definitions: To extract or remove something from a place or container.
To withdraw from an activity, agreement, or commitment.
To move away from the side of the road or a queue of traffic.
To leave a station or stop (for a train or bus).
examples: She had to pull out a splinter from her finger.
The company decided to pull out of the deal at the last minute.
The car pulled out into the main road.
The train is about to pull out.
